comment: Inputs for build_stock.py. Curve/spectrum entries are points CSVs relative to tools/digitize/. midGreyLogExposure: the 'Camera Stops 0' tick (x = 445.9 pt) on the 7219 sensitometric graph lines up with log E -1.50 on the top LOG EXPOSURE axis calibrated by its frame-edge labels -4.0 and 1.0 (0 stops is exactly mid-frame). Reading the irregular local top ticks (-2.0 at 425.5, -1.0 at 462.0 pt) instead gives -1.44; see figures/7219_sensitometry.json.

sources.title: KODAK VISION3 500T Color Negative Film 5219 / 7219 / SO-219, Technical Data H-1-5219t (Revised 7-15)

ASSUMPTION: base thickness 0.127 mm (5 mil cellulose-triacetate camera-negative base). Britannica gives 0.08-0.2 mm as the typical photographic base range; no Kodak datasheet figure for 5219 was found.
sources.note: Typical range only; 0.127 mm is the assumed value.

sources.title: ASSUMPTION: reflectanceOff 0.29 = diffuse internal reflectance of a base/air interface, 1 - (1 - 0.092)/n^2 with n = 1.48 (cellulose triacetate), about 0.585, times an assumed 0.5 ratio of red light reaching the base to red light absorbed in the emulsion.
sources.note: No published rem-jet-off reflectance was found. Searches (halation literature, Kodak AHU talking points) describe the mechanism only: rem-jet absorbs light before it reflects off the rear base surface.

sources.title: ASSUMPTION: reflectanceOn 0.01 (carbon-black rem-jet leaves about 1 % of the light returned).
sources.note: Source describes the rem-jet layer's purpose; the 1 % figure is assumed. Note Kodak VISION3 replaced rem-jet with an emulsion-side anti-halation undercoat (https://theasc.com/article/kodak-enhances-vision3/); 'on' is used as the stand-in for that stock's as-shipped state.

sources.title: layerSplit is derived by build_stock.py from this stock's linear layer sensitivities over 600-700 nm, not typed in.
